A1.justification: Both PDFs present ReservoirTTA with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–K. All 34 pages were compared in text and rendered form; differences are confined to pages 1 and 12.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and semantic-segmentation experiments in Section 5, plus ablations, qualitative examples and additional quantitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including classification results in Tables 1–2, segmentation results in Table 3 and additional evaluations in Appendix K.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain identical style-based domain identification, reservoir initialization, selective adaptation and parameter-ensemble prediction procedures. The temporally correlated-stream adaptation in Appendix K is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10/100-C, ImageNet-C, continuously changing corruptions and Cityscapes-to-ACDC segmentation. Recurring CSC/CDC scenarios and Appendix K's temporally correlated test streams are retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding main-text and appendix experiments, including CoLA and DPCore in the ViT comparisons, BECoTTA in segmentation and RoTTA in Table 21.

E3.justification: The twenty-visit CSC/CDC evaluations, CCC adaptation windows, ten-cycle segmentation evaluations, metrics, backbones and Table 8 settings are unchanged. Table 21 retains the same temporal-correlation protocol.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 4, style-feature and clustering analyses in Appendices D–F, sensitivity studies in Appendix I and qualitative examples in Appendix J are identical.

E5.justification: Five-run/seed averaging, the five batch-order seeds used in Figure 16 and existing variability summaries are unchanged. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical-estimation procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains 51.0% ImageNet-C error for EATA+ReservoirTTA at visit 20 under recurring CSC.

T1.justification: Section 3's assumptions, stability-region definition and variance/divergence results, Appendix B's proofs and derivations, and the method equations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The scientific claims about domain-specialized adaptation, style-based discovery, theoretical stability and prolonged adaptation performance remain identical in the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: Interpretations of specialization, regularization and recurring-domain behavior are unchanged. The computational-overhead limitation and the small-batch and temporally correlated-stream qualifications are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an abstract statement that the authors' code is publicly available and identifies the LTS5/ReservoirTTA GitHub repository, absent from v1. This adds project-specific access information; implementation settings and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and research positioning are unchanged. Reference [33] replaces arXiv metadata with an ICLR venue entry for the same authors and title, constituting only a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a code-availability sentence, reference [33]'s bibliographic wording changes and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining prose and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence produces slight first-page reflow and spacing adjustments, while reference [33] is locally retypeset on page 12. All figures, tables and appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies a project-specific code-availability statement and repository address absent from v1, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. The scientific content and appendices are unchanged. The demonstrated gain concerns documented access; the PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability.
